text:
**Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") is now on Hugging Face, and its cybersecurity results stand out. 🛡️**

On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index task that asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it, Mistral Large 4 scores **82%**, the highest reported score on that test. According to Mistral, several closed frontier models score near zero on the same task because they refuse to attempt it.

That matters for defenders, because you usually can't fix a vulnerability without first reproducing it.

**Why open weights matter for security teams:**
🔹 Legitimate incident response and vulnerability research often look like attacks, so closed-API filters can block them.
🔹 If your workflow depends on an API, you can lose access in the middle of an incident.
🔹 With open weights, your team controls both the deployment and the usage policy.
🔹 Researchers can measure refusal behavior directly instead of relying on a provider's description.

The model isn't a free-for-all, though. On harmful cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is higher than any other open-weight model's.

**Key specs:**
• ~1T total parameters, ~49B active (Mixture-of-Experts, 128 experts + 1 shared)
• 1M-token context window
• Multimodal: text + images in, text out (1.6B Pixtral vision encoder)
• Two kinds of sparsity: MoE routing selects which experts run, and a DeepSeek Sparse Attention indexer selects which context positions to attend to

**Benchmark highlights:**
📊 Cybench: 93% of 40 security-competition challenges
📊 Coding Agent Index: 49.8%, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max
📊 Lakera B3: 93.3% resistance to prompt injection
📊 #5 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

**Day-0 support** in Transformers, vLLM, llama.cpp and TRL, plus Inference Endpoints and Dell Enterprise Hub recipes. The 2-bit GGUF quants run on a single 512GB Apple Silicon Ultra machine.

There's also a fine-tuning opportunity. Reproduce-then-patch tasks have a verifiable reward, so they fit naturally into RL environments. Teams could use Mistral Large 4's traces to train smaller, specialized security models on their own codebases.

One caveat: it ships under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, an MIT derivative that restricts model-as-a-service offerings. Check the terms before you build a product on it.

Would your security team run a model like this in-house? 👇

*Note: The article lists ~49B active parameters, but the model ID is `Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`, which suggests 52B. The gap may come from counting the vision encoder and shared components. You may want to confirm which figure Mistral uses before posting.*
